```{r}
#| include: false
# Slides read saved outputs from R/LTU-team.R (run that first). No downloads at render time.
library(dplyr); library(tidyr); library(ggplot2); library(stringr); library(scales); library(readr)
theme_set(theme_minimal(base_size = 18))
teal <- "#3F8F84"; orange <- "#E07830"

pairs <- read_csv("Outputs/tables/LTU_final_pair_connection_table.csv") |>
  mutate(across(c(player_1, player_2), str_squish))

cent <- read_csv("Outputs/tables/LTU_centrality_player.csv") |>
  mutate(player_name = str_squish(player_name))


# One consistent label per player across both datasets
player_names <- sort(unique(c(
  pairs$player_1,
  pairs$player_2,
  cent$player_name
)))
player_names <- player_names[
  !is.na(player_names) & nzchar(player_names)
]

player_labels <- setNames(
  paste("Player", seq_along(player_names)),
  player_names
)

pairs <- pairs |>
  mutate(
    player_1 = unname(player_labels[player_1]),
    player_2 = unname(player_labels[player_2])
  )

cent <- cent |>
  mutate(player_name = unname(player_labels[player_name]))
```

## Points and plus-minus can't show who plays well *together*

- Results also depend on teammates, opponents and minutes played
- Individual stats say who is good, not which combinations work

::: {.callout-note}
## Question
Which LTU pairings create more value than their individual ratings would predict?
:::

## Data: 10 LTU games, 8 usable

- UBL women's 2025 play-by-play: substitutions, shots, game clock, player IDs (UniSport / Sportradar feed)
- 2 of 10 games dropped: lineup tracking failed when a starter had no logged action before the first substitution
- Final scores for all 61 league games, used only for the league context at the end

## From raw events to a connection score

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-height: 2.5
#| out-width: "95%"
#| fig-align: center

steps <- data.frame(
  id = 1:5,
  title = c("Lineups", "Stints", "RAPM", "Pair score", "Stability"),
  line1 = c("Reconstruct", "Same-lineup", "Ridge model",
            "Actual minus", "Leave one game"),
  line2 = c("on-court five", "intervals", "per stint",
            "predicted", "out, rescore"),
  group = c(rep("Data preparation", 2),
            rep("Modelling and validation", 3))
)

box_w <- 1.8
gap <- 0.4

steps$xmin <- (steps$id - 1) * (box_w + gap)
steps$xmax <- steps$xmin + box_w
steps$xmid <- (steps$xmin + steps$xmax) / 2

arrows <- data.frame(
  x = steps$xmax[1:4] + 0.04,
  xend = steps$xmin[2:5] - 0.04,
  y = 0.75,
  yend = 0.75
)

ggplot() +
  geom_rect(
    data = steps,
    aes(xmin = xmin, xmax = xmax,
        ymin = 0, ymax = 1.5, fill = group)
  ) +
  geom_text(
    data = steps,
    aes(x = xmid, y = 1.12, label = title),
    colour = "white", fontface = "bold", size = 5.5
  ) +
  geom_text(
    data = steps,
    aes(x = xmid, y = 0.72, label = line1),
    colour = "white", size = 4
  ) +
  geom_text(
    data = steps,
    aes(x = xmid, y = 0.38, label = line2),
    colour = "white", size = 4
  ) +
  geom_segment(
    data = arrows,
    aes(x = x, xend = xend, y = y, yend = yend),
    arrow = grid::arrow(
      length = grid::unit(0.16, "cm"),
      type = "closed"
    ),
    colour = "grey40"
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c(
      "Data preparation" = teal,
      "Modelling and validation" = orange
    ),
    name = NULL
  ) +
  coord_cartesian(
    xlim = c(-0.1, max(steps$xmax) + 0.1),
    ylim = c(-0.05, 1.55),
    expand = FALSE
  ) +
  theme_void(base_size = 13) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.key.size = grid::unit(0.35, "cm"),
    legend.margin = margin(0, 0, 0, 0),
    plot.margin = margin(0, 0, 0, 0)
  )
```

::: {style="font-size: 0.75em;"}

**Lineup prediction**
$$
y_s = \beta_0 + \sum_p \beta_p x_{sp}
      + \sum_o \delta_o z_{so} + \varepsilon_s
$$

**Connection score**
$$
C_{ij} =
\frac{\sum_{s \ni i,j} d_s (y_s - \hat{y}_s)}
     {\sum_{s \ni i,j} d_s}
$$

:::

::: notes
Walk left to right, one sentence per box.

The model predicts net points per minute using the players on court
and the opponent team.

The connection score averages the prediction errors from stints
where both players played, weighted by stint length.

A positive score means the team performed better than predicted
during their shared minutes. It is an adjusted association,
not proof of personal chemistry.
:::

## Some pairs outperform what their lineups predict

```{r}
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 5.6
#| out-width: "100%"
#| fig-align: center
plot_df <- bind_rows(
  slice_max(pairs, connection_score, n = 5, with_ties = FALSE),
  slice_min(pairs, connection_score, n = 5, with_ties = FALSE)
) |>
    mutate(label = sprintf("%s + %s (%.0f min, %d games)", player_1, player_2,
                         minutes_together, n_games_together),
         label = reorder(label, connection_score))
ggplot(plot_df, aes(connection_score, label, fill = stability)) +
  geom_col() + geom_vline(xintercept = 0) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Stable positive" = teal, "Stable negative" = orange,
                               "Uncertain" = "grey60", "Insufficient stability evidence" = "grey85"),
                    name = "Leave-one-game-out") +
  labs(x = "Connection score (net points per minute above prediction)", y = NULL) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

Top and bottom 5 of 73 pairs (at least 15 minutes, 2 games).
An association, not proof of chemistry.

## Do the scores generalise? Not detectably

```{r}
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 4.6
pg <- read.csv("Outputs/tables/LTU_prediction_per_game.csv") |> mutate(game = factor(row_number()))
ggplot(pg, aes(y = game)) +
  geom_segment(aes(x = rmse_baseline, xend = rmse_enhanced, yend = game), colour = "grey60") +
  geom_point(aes(x = rmse_baseline, colour = "Baseline"), size = 4) +
  geom_point(aes(x = rmse_enhanced, colour = "With pair scores"), size = 4) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("Baseline" = "grey40", "With pair scores" = orange), name = NULL) +
  labs(x = "Prediction error, weighted RMSE (lower is better)", y = "Held-out game") +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

Scores fitted on 7 games, tested on the 8th: RMSE 2.30 vs 2.30, better in 4 of 8 games, permutation p = 0.22.

::: notes
(1 min) This is the honest test. The scores describe the games they came from; no evidence yet they persist. A null result with 225 stints and a noisy outcome is expected, not a failure.
:::

## Takeaways

1. Pair scores flag combinations worth a closer look
2. The rotation is broadly connected; bridging sits with two heavily used players
3. Held-out testing found no evidence the scores persist, so treat them as hypotheses for coaches

::: {.smaller}
Limits: one season, 8 games, minutes rather than possessions. Next: more games and seasons.
:::

::: notes
(1 min) End broad: small-sample sports analytics needs out-of-sample checks before names are attached to effects. Then invite questions.
:::

## Bridging is concentrated in two heavily used players

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="55%"}
```{r}
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 5.5

ggplot(cent, aes(weighted_betweenness, reorder(player_name, weighted_betweenness), fill = weighted_strength)) +
  geom_col() +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "grey85", high = teal, name = "Shared minutes") +
  labs(x = "Weighted betweenness", y = NULL)
```
:::
::: {.column width="45%"}
- 112 of 120 possible pairs shared the court
- All 8 gaps involve four players with only 3 to 4 games and under 53 minutes
- Minutes are spread fairly evenly (Gini 0.27), bridging is not (Gini 0.88)
:::
:::

::: notes
(1 min) Betweenness looks like tactical importance but is mostly exposure: the most-used players are the likeliest link to the rarely used ones.
:::

## Stability and data quality

- Leave-one-game-out: drop a game, refit, record whether each pair stays positive (at least 80% = stable)
- Quarter-break lineups are carried over; discrepancies were flagged, not corrected

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| eval: false
# Connection score: duration-weighted mean stint residual per pair
stint_resid <- actual_net_per_minute - predicted_net_per_minute
weighted.mean(stint_resid, w = duration_sec)
```

## Centrality measures

- Strength: total shared minutes. Betweenness: lies on short paths between others (more minutes = shorter distance)
- Eigenvector: connected to well-connected players. Gini: concentration, 0 equal to 1 concentrated

## 
**Lineup prediction**
$$
y_s = \beta_0 + \sum_p \beta_p x_{sp}
      + \sum_o \delta_o z_{so} + \varepsilon_s
$$

**Connection score**
$$
C_{ij} =
\frac{\sum_{s \ni i,j} d_s (y_s - \hat{y}_s)}
     {\sum_{s \ni i,j} d_s}
$$

$y_s$: net points per minute in stint $s$; $x_{sp}$: player $p$ on court; $z_{so}$: opponent; $d_s$: stint length; $\hat{y}_s$: model prediction



## How team eigenvector centrality is calculated

::: {style="font-size: 0.75em;"}

- Each node is a team; arrows point **loser → winner**.
- Edge weights are winning margins.
- Beating highly central teams contributes more to the score.

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="45%"}

$$
c_i = \frac{1}{\lambda}\sum_j A_{ji}c_j
$$

:::
::: {.column width="55%"}

| Symbol | Meaning |
|--------|---------|
| $c_i$ | Centrality of team $i$ |
| $c_j$ | Centrality of defeated team $j$ |
| $A_{ji}$ | Total winning margin on arrows $j \to i$ |
| $\lambda$ | Associated eigenvalue |

:::
:::

**Scaling:** highest score = 1.  
**Gini:** measures concentration of the scores across teams.

:::

::: notes
Centrality is not a win percentage or official league position.
Lambda here is an eigenvalue, not the RAPM ridge penalty.
:::
